question: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mughal Emperor Jahangir issued silver coins in honor of his beloved wife, Mehrunnisa, who was also known as Nur Jahan.
 
• These coins were unique as they carried the name of the queen, which was an uncommon practice in Mughal coinage.
 
• Nur Jahan was a powerful influence in Jahangir's court and had a significant role in administrative matters.
 
• The coins symbolized Jahangir's deep affection and respect for Nur Jahan, highlighting her prominence in the Mughal empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nur Jahan**

 
 
• Born as Mehrunnisa, she was the twentieth and most beloved wife of Emperor Jahangir.
 
• She was a highly educated and influential woman, known for her administrative acumen and architectural patronage.
 
• Nur Jahan effectively wielded power and was one of the few Mughal women who left a significant mark on the empire's history.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Coinage**
 
 
• Mughal coinage was known for its artistic excellence and intricate designs.
 
• Coins issued by Jahangir often depicted his interest in various arts and his deep affection for Nur Jahan.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir's Reign**
 
 
• Jahangir ruled from 1605 to 1627 and was known for his patronage of the arts.
 
• His reign was marked by a relatively stable administration and flourishing cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Mughal Empire**
 
 
• Women like Nur Jahan played crucial roles in the Mughal court, influencing politics and culture.
 
• Their contributions were often commemorated through various means, including coinage and architecture.
